guideTitle: 6 Best Grab Bars With Towel Racks in 2026
metaTitle: Best Grab Bars With Towel Racks in 2026
metaDescription: Six grab bar and towel rack combos compared by length, tube size, capacity and finish, for showers where towels need to be within easy reach.
introParagraphs: A towel bar that doubles as a grab bar puts a handhold exactly where a person reaches when stepping out of the shower, and that is the whole appeal. It also cleans up the wall, since you hang a towel on the same fixture you might lean on. The catch is that a towel rack and a grab bar are built to different standards, and the listings are not equally clear about which job each does best.

This lineup covers the Moen 24-inch bar with a towel bar rated to 500 lb, the Healthcraft Plus 24-inch combo with a 9-hole flange, the iHansee brushed nickel 24-inch bar, the Delta 24-inch polished chrome combo with a slim 7/8-inch tube, the Ciao Stilista bar-and-rack set at 16 and 25 inches and the Zepolu black 17-inch bar with a 1.25-inch tube.

We evaluated each on tube size, capacity wording, mounting design and how the towel function is built, because a towel hanging on the bar can hide the grip or add load. Where a listing states its limits, we use them, and where it does not, we say so.

products.name: Moen 24 Inch Grab Bar With Towel Bar, Brushed Nickel

specList.label: Listed capacity
specList.value: 500 lb in a stud or with SecureMounts

products.description:
Moen's LR2350 is a 24-inch grab bar with a convenient towel bar built in, finished in a lightly brushed warm-gray nickel. The listing says it supports up to 500 lb when installed in a stud or when using SecureMounts, which are not included, and that Moen designs the bar for hassle-free installation. It is the combination bar with the clearest stated capacity in the group.

The design makes sense in daily use. The towel sits on the outside, the hand grips the bar proper, and the whole fixture lives next to the shower entrance. A well-built combo also means one set of screws and one flange pattern to plan around, which simplifies a tiled wall.

Compared with the Delta 24-inch it lists a far higher capacity and a thicker grip as far as the text shows, since the Delta tube is 7/8 inch. Compared with the Healthcraft it is a plainer, brand-backed option. It is the pick when you want a recognizable name, a nickel finish and a capacity statement you can plan around.
products.bestFor: A shower entrance wall with a clear capacity statement.
pros: 500 lb stated in a stud or with SecureMounts
24 in length gives several hand positions
Towel bar built into the fixture
cons: Needs studs for the top rating
Towels can cover part of the grip

products.name: Healthcraft Plus 24 Inch Towel Bar and Grab Bar, 500 lb
products.description:
Healthcraft sells a designer towel bar that is also a 24-inch ADA-style grab bar, with a listed 500 lb capacity in number 304 stainless steel that the listing calls rust-resistant and waterproof. It uses concealed screws and the brand's proprietary 9-hole flanges, which are meant to make installation more manageable. The look is modern and clean.

The 9-hole flange is the practical highlight. In a bathroom where the studs are not where you want the bar, more holes mean more ways to line up with framing and fewer compromises on position. Concealed screws give a tidy appearance, though they mean you should align carefully before the cover goes on.

Compared with the iHansee bar it is a more premium, design-led piece, and compared with the Moen it adds a flange system. It suits a bathroom remodel where the towel bar is meant to be seen and the install is the uncertain part, and where you are comfortable paying for design.
products.bestFor: Remodels where the bar is on view and studs are awkward.
cons: Designer pricing tier relative to others
Towel and grip share one bar
Style may not suit every bathroom

products.name: iHansee Brushed Nickel 24 Inch Grab Bar With Towel Holder
products.description:
iHansee's bar is a 24-inch brushed nickel unit in 304 stainless steel that the listing describes as two purposes in one: a sturdy grab bar and a towel rack. The pitch is practical, since towels end up within easy reach when you step out of the tub or shower. It is a no-frills combination.

The listing does not give a capacity number in the text we have, so confirm it on the product page before relying on it for heavy support. The nickel finish is easy to live with and matches many fixtures, and 304 stainless is a reasonable material for a wet room.

Compared with the Moen it makes fewer capacity claims, and compared with the Healthcraft it has fewer design extras. Compared with the polished chrome iHansee version, this one is the warmer finish, so the choice is about fixtures. It is a straightforward pick for a household that wants a clean, nickel, dual-use bar without paying for a premium name.
products.bestFor: A simple nickel combo bar for a family bathroom.
cons: No capacity figure in the text we have
Towel use can hide the grip

products.name: Ciao Stilista 16 Inch Grab Bar With 25 Inch Towel Rack
products.description:
Ciao Stilista gives you a different layout: a 16-inch grab bar with a separate 25-inch towel rack as one unit, so the rack carries the towel while the shorter bar carries the hand. The listing claims a 500 lb grab bar capacity, citing a thicker internal plate and a 1.25-inch solid steel tube, and says the stainless is real 304 that will not rust. Its tone is promotional, so read the numbers as the maker's claims.

Separating the rack from the bar is a sensible idea, because a wet towel on the grip is a nuisance. The 1.25-inch tube is a comfortable hand size, and the longer rack holds a bath towel without bunching. The unit is larger on the wall than a single bar.

Compared with the Moen it puts the towel on its own rail, and compared with the Zepolu it is longer overall. It suits a shower with plenty of wall space and a household that wants the towel and the handhold kept apart.
products.bestFor: Keeping the towel off the part you grip.
pros: Separate 25 in towel rack from the grip bar
cons: Needs studs for the top rating

products.name: Zepolu Black 17 Inch Towel Grab Bar, 1.25 Inch Tube
products.description:
Zepolu offers a 17-inch matte black bar that combines a grab bar and a towel bar in one piece, made from 304 stainless steel with 1.25-inch tubing. The listing says it is resistant to rust, corrosion and tarnish, and that it is built to last in a shower. The shorter length suits smaller walls and fits a modern bathroom with black fixtures.

A 17-inch bar will hold a hand towel or a folded bath towel, but not a long hanging one. That makes it a better fit for a small shower or a vanity-side wall. The black finish is on-trend, and as with any coating it is worth handling gently.

Compared with the 24-inch bars here it is shorter and holds less, and compared with the Ciao Stilista it is a single bar rather than a bar-and-rack unit. It is the pick for a compact, black-fixture bathroom where a short dual-purpose bar is enough.
cons: Shorter, so holds a smaller towel
Capacity is not stated in the text we have
Black coating can scratch over time

products.name: Delta 41519 24 Inch Towel Bar and Grab Bar Combo, Chrome
specs: Towel bar doubles as assist bar
products.description:
Delta's combo is a 24-inch towel bar that also functions as an assist bar, with a 7/8-inch diameter and a 3-inch projection from the wall in polished chrome. The slim tube is the defining detail: it is considerably thinner than the 1.25-inch bars elsewhere in this guide, and it holds a towel neatly. The listing is brief, with no capacity figure in the text we have.

That slimness is a tradeoff. A slimmer bar blends in as a towel bar and can suit smaller hands, but it gives less to wrap fingers around, and a person who relies on a firm grip may find it too thin. The 3-inch projection leaves room for fingers behind the bar and a towel in front.

Compared with the Moen and Healthcraft bars, this is more of a towel bar with assist ability than a dedicated grab bar. It suits a household that wants a stylish chrome towel bar that can offer a steadying touch, but not a person who needs to lean heavily on the fixture.
products.bestFor: A steadying touch from a good-looking chrome towel bar.
pros: 24 in towel bar doubles as an assist bar
Slim 7/8 in tube suits small hands
cons: Slim tube gives less to hold
No capacity figure in the text we have
More towel bar than dedicated grab bar

buyingCriteria.criterion: Grab bar first or towel bar first
buyingCriteria.explanation: Combination fixtures lean one way or the other. The Moen LR2350 states 500 lb and reads as a grab bar with a towel function, while the Delta 41519 with its 7/8-inch tube reads as a towel bar with assist ability. Decide which job matters more before you buy. If someone will lean on it daily, choose the grab-bar-first design. Hold the product dimensions against your wall with painter's tape before you commit.

The Ciao Stilista and Zepolu list 1.25-inch tubes, a comfortable size for many hands, while the Delta is 7/8 inch. A slim tube is easier to wrap with a towel and looks lighter but gives a firmer grip less well. Hold a similar-size object at home to judge. Diameter matters most for people with weaker hands. A bar that is a pleasure to hold will actually get used, which matters more than a headline rating.

A towel draped over the grip can hide it and make it slippery. The Ciao Stilista separates a 25-inch rack from a 16-inch bar so the towel never covers the handle. On a single-bar design like the Moen, drape the towel off to one side or hang it where the hand does not grip. Think about how you will actually use it. If the towel often ends up draped over the bar, the Ciao Stilista layout is worth the extra wall space.

The Moen and Healthcraft state 500 lb, the Ciao Stilista claims 500 lb for its grab bar and the Delta and iHansee state none in the text we have. Capacity assumes studs or rated anchors, so plan the mount first. Towel weight is small, but a person's weight is not. Do not treat a towel bar as a grab bar unless the listing says it is one. Remember that towel weight is trivial, and the real question is whether the bar can take a person's weight.

The Healthcraft 9-hole flange helps align with studs, and the Moen mounts into a stud or with SecureMounts. Towel bars often sit near the shower entrance, where studs may be inconvenient. A flexible flange reduces compromises. Mark the stud locations before choosing a bar length. On a tiled wall, check the flange hole pattern against your stud spacing before ordering.

A 24-inch bar holds a folded bath towel, while the 17-inch Zepolu is better for hand towels. A longer bar also gives more hand positions. Measure your wall and check clearance from the showerhead and door. Make sure the swing of a shower door does not hit the bar. Check the swing of the shower door and the position of the showerhead arm before settling on 24 inches.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dual-function design
howWeEvaluated.description: We examined how each unit combines a towel function with a grip, from the Moen single bar to the Ciao Stilista separate rack. We asked whether a towel would interfere with the grip. Designs that kept the two jobs distinct earned credit. We looked closely at how each listing separates the towel function from the support function.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the Moen and Healthcraft 500 lb statements and the Ciao Stilista claim against the lack of a figure on the Delta and iHansee listings. Numbers tied to installation scored higher. A towel bar without a stated capacity was treated as a towel bar first. We treated a missing capacity figure as a reason to ask questions, not as proof of weakness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tube and hand fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Diameters from 7/8 to 1.25 inches were compared. We weighed the comfort of a thicker tube against the look of a slim one. The Delta slim tube was flagged for people who need a firm grip. The 7/8 inch tube on the Delta was assessed as a style choice with a grip tradeoff.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mounting design
howWeEvaluated.description: The Healthcraft 9-hole flange, the Moen SecureMount option and concealed screw designs were compared. We looked for features that help in tiled walls. Clear mounting information was credited. We favored flange designs that help a household with no special tools.

howWeEvaluated.title: Finish and match
howWeEvaluated.description: Brushed nickel, polished chrome, stainless and matte black were compared for how they would blend with typical fixtures and how they would clean. Finish choice was considered part of daily use. Finish was judged for how it behaves next to damp towels, which can leave marks on softer coatings.

faq.q: Can I use a towel bar as a grab bar?
faq.a: Only if the listing says it is designed for that. The Moen and Healthcraft combos state 500 lb, while the Delta 41519 is described as a towel bar that also functions as an assist bar without a stated capacity in the text we have. A regular towel bar is not built for body weight and can pull out of the wall. If the listing for a towel bar never mentions a weight rating, assume it is meant for towels and nothing more.

faq.q: How do I choose between a single bar and a bar with a separate rack?
faq.a: A single bar saves wall space and costs less, while a bar-and-rack unit like the Ciao Stilista keeps towels off the grip. If the grip is used daily, the separate rack is a nice touch. In a small shower, a single bar is usually easier to fit. Ask yourself whether the grip will be used daily; if so, the separate rack design is the more considerate layout.

faq.q: Does a towel on the bar make it unsafe?
faq.a: A towel can cover the part of the bar you grip and make it slippery. Hang the towel to one side or use a unit with a separate rack. Always grip the bare tube when you need support. Wipe the tube dry before gripping it after a shower, since a damp towel can leave fabric lint and moisture on the surface.

faq.q: What tube diameter should I choose?
faq.a: Most people find 1.25 inches comfortable, as on the Zepolu and Ciao Stilista. The Delta at 7/8 inch is slimmer and better suited to light touch than a firm hold. If you have weak hands, avoid very slim tubes. Try holding a rolling pin or a similar handle to feel the difference between a slim and a standard tube.

Beside the shower entrance at a height where your hand lands naturally, usually near waist level. Mark the spot with tape and mime the movement before drilling. Make sure the shower door will not hit the bar. A quick tape test with a tape measure and a helper will show whether the door swing, the shower arm and your elbow all have room.

faq.q: How do I install it in tile?
faq.a: Find studs with a stud finder, mark the flange holes and use a tile or glass bit with slow speed. Seal around the screws and follow the maker's instructions. If you are unsure, a handyperson can do it quickly. A slow, light touch on the drill is the safest approach with tile, and a sealant bead afterward keeps moisture out of the wall.
